about: Reaction, metabolic and mechanistic schemes drawn on Dr. Sikazwe's assigned Exam 1 pages of f26-DEENT-DPAW-mc.pdf (file pages 7-9, 12, 15-23, 25-34, 43-55, 61-66; his list of 11/06). gen_reactions.py draws every species with RDKit from the SMILES here and writes reactions.js; verify_reactions.py checks every species against PubChem (and ChEMBL where an id is known) with the Atlas's verify_pubchem.py logic and writes verification/reactions_verification.json. A species with an `atlas` key uses the Atlas item's SMILES (reactions_check.js enforces it). `verify_smiles` replaces a drawing's attachment atom (DNA) for the PubChem lookup. Slide = PDF page. T = 11/03 lecture-only transcript line; T@ = character offset in the 11/04 transcript.

species.name: Pre-vitamin D3
species.source: Not drawn on slide 27: the assigned reading (Bikle, Endotext 2025, Overview: UV "breaks the B ring to form pre-D3. Pre-D3 isomerizes to D3"); PubChem CID 5281058 (previtamin D3).

species.name: Anthranyl radical
species.note: The slide labels it "Anthranyl radical" and draws the anthralin skeleton; the radical centre is drawn here at C-10, the CH2 that anthralin loses a hydrogen from.

species.name: Psoralen
species.note: Slide 18 draws psoralen itself in the scheme; the drug in the box beside it, 8-MOP (methoxsalen), carries an 8-OCH3.

species.name: Thymine (on a DNA strand)
species.note: N1 carries the DNA strand (drawn as a wavy line on the slide, "DNA" here); the base itself is checked as thymine.

species.name: Psoralen–thymine interstrand diadduct
species.note: Two cyclobutane rings: the pyrone C3=C4 and the furan C4'=C5' double bonds each add to a thymine C5=C6 double bond, as slide 18 draws it; no stereochemistry is shown on the slide, so none is drawn. Checked with N1-methyl groups in place of the DNA strands.

species.name: Salicyluric acid (glycine conjugate)
species.note: Not drawn on the slide, which prints "?" after AA-Conjugation; drawn from the product he named aloud, the glycine conjugate (11/04 T@22430–@22480).

species.name: Benzoyl radical
species.note: The slide labels it "Benzoyl radical" and draws PhC(=O)O· (the benzoyloxy radical), as the Atlas tile does.

figures.title: Crisaborole: hydrolysis, oxidation, conjugation
figures.caption: After DPAW slide 9 (Polleve-1; the steps numbered as printed there) and slide 7. The slide prints no enzyme names; the enzymes in the step captions are the ones he named in lecture (11/03 T 699–711, 766–776). The conjugates are drawn as the slide draws them: the SO<sub>3</sub> or Gluc tag beside a bracket over both OH groups, the position not specified.

figures.title: Hydrocortisone metabolism
figures.caption: After DPAW slide 26 (printed 25), arrows and enzyme labels as printed; ⇌ marks the slide's paired arrows. In lecture he dwelt on the 11β-HSD step: hydrocortisone “ping pongs” with cortisone, its major metabolite, by oxidation and reduction (11/03 T 1189–1196); the 11 is carbon 11 (11/04 T@650–@800). The 5β-reductase and 3α-HSD steps are on the slide, in its highlighted box.

figures.title: Vitamin D3: 7-dehydrocholesterol to calcitriol
figures.caption: Steps 1–4 are DPAW slide 27 (printed 26) as printed, with its blanks (“reaction??”, “organ??”) left open so you can answer them yourself. Step 5 is not on the slide: it fills the blanks from the reading he assigned (Bikle, “Vitamin D: Production, Metabolism, and Mechanism of Action”, Endotext, linked on slide 2), which he made the source of a 2-point question: “I'm gonna have two points, a question with two points based on that” (11/03 T 603–606); identify the reaction, the organs and the enzymes (11/04 T@2873–@4440). In class he gave only the enzyme 1-α-hydroxylase (printed) and said that light is involved in the first step (T@4371).

figures.title: Anthralin autoxidation
figures.caption: After DPAW slide 17. Spontaneous autoxidation, no enzyme: one electron (e) passes to oxygen, giving superoxide anion and the anthranyl radical, the two cytotoxic radicals of its CBDA (11/03 T 928–945). The radicals polymerize to anthralin brown and carbon black, the stains, which are not part of the treatment (T 946–953). The slide's drawing of carbon black is not redrawn here.

figures.title: Psoralen + UVA: DNA crosslink
figures.caption: After DPAW slide 18. The psoralen intercalates between DNA base pairs; UVA light then activates its pyrone and furan double bonds, each of which adds to a thymine (pyrimidine) double bond, so the two DNA strands are crosslinked and DNA synthesis stops (11/03 T 961–976). The slide draws psoralen itself; the drug, 8-MOP (methoxsalen), carries an 8-OCH<sub>3</sub>.

figures.title: Folate reduction by DHFR
figures.caption: After DPAW slide 30 (printed 29), the arrow labelled as printed. Methotrexate sits in the same DHFR cavity and competes with folic acid, so less tetrahydrofolic acid is made for DNA synthesis (slide 30; 11/04 T@8850–@9000).

figures.title: Apremilast metabolism
figures.caption: After DPAW slide 34 (printed 33), as printed: the metabolites are boxes, not structures. CYP3A4 (major; 1A2 and 2A6 minor) O-demethylates it; the OH metabolite is then glucuronidated by UGTs (slide 34; 11/04 T@14063–@14300).

figures.title: Glycolic and salicylic acid metabolism
figures.caption: After DPAW slide 43 (printed 42), arrow labels as printed. Step 2 fills the slide's “?” with the product he named aloud, the glycine conjugate (11/04 T@22430–@22480); the slide does not draw it. Glycolic acid: two enzymes, alcohol dehydrogenase and aldehyde dehydrogenase (T@20818–@21000).

figures.title: Benzoyl peroxide in the skin
figures.caption: After DPAW slide 47 (printed 46). The peroxide bond breaks: benzoic acid lowers skin pH (keratolytic) and the benzoyl radical kills bacteria (11/04 T@25800–@26300). The slide labels the radical “benzoyl radical” and draws PhC(=O)O·, as here.

figures.title: Etretinate to acitretin
figures.caption: After DPAW slide 50 (printed 49). The slide's arrow is unlabelled; “CEs” is what he said: etretinate, the ethyl ester prodrug, is bioactivated by carboxylesterases to acitretin, the active form used directly since etretinate left the market (11/04 T@28850–@29700).

figures.title: Tazarotene to tazarotenic acid
figures.caption: After DPAW slide 51 (printed 50). The slide labels the arrow “??”; his answer: tazarotene is an ester prodrug hydrolyzed by carboxylesterases (CE) to tazarotenic acid (11/04 T@7013–@7120, @30227–@30300).
